newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power steady amid warm weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power steady amid warm weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. finished Tuesday mostly steady from Monday's level, stablizing after Monday's weakness due to return of two Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) nuclear units.
Outlook for slightly higher than normal temperatures in most of the region for much of week helped support prices, marketers and traders said.
"The weather forecast is 70s (Fahrenheit) through Friday and Saturday," said a Florida trader, referring to the outlook of the daily peak temperature range.
"The Georgia/Florida interface got filled in pretty quickly," the trader said, noting transmission tightness to move power into the Florida pennisula.
Within Florida, hourly power prices were pegged near $30.00 a megawatt hour, and electricity prescheduled in eight to 10 hour blocks for Wednesday was fetched in the $27.00-$29.00 range.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Wednesday delivery was again quoted at $21.00-$22.50 a megawatt hour (MWh).
Firm, off-peak power for Wednesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally valued at $15.00-$17.00, higher than Monday's $14.00-$15.00.
In the northwestern part of TVA's (TVA) territory, firm, peak electricity for Wednesday delivery was assessed at $17.00-$18.00, off from Monday's $18.00-$20.00.
Firm, next-day power for delivery into northwestern TVA during light load hours on Wednesday was held steady at $12.00-$14.00.
TVA was heard offering next-day, non-firm electricity for peak hours at $21.50, and for off-peak hours at $17.00.

TVA's 1,065 MW Browns Ferry 2 nuclear power unit in Decatur, Ala., and 1,148 MW Sequoyah nuclear unit 2 in Soddy Daisy, Tenn., were restarted this past weekend. Browns Ferry 2 reached full output late Monday, and Sequoyah 2 was operating at 30 percent of capacity.
